newsitem.title: FRANCE: French start to catch Internet, multimedia craze.
newsitem.headline: French start to catch Internet, multimedia craze.

text.p: The French have been slow to catch the Internet/multimedia bug but nearly a fifth plan to connect in the next two years and buy multimedia equipment, a recent study showed.

The study, published late last month by measurement institute Publimetrie and educational television channel La Cinquieme, found just two percent of people questioned are connected to the Internet at home and only seven percent use it at work.
But 18 percent said they envisaged getting hooked up in the next two years, planning to spend on average 9,554 francs each on equipment and 2,893 francs each on programmes.
"It's much better than last year... there has been a small take-off," said Christophe Excoffier, Publimetrie's studies director.
Excoffier said the French Internet and multimedia market had become more fixed, with market positions carved out.
"We have moved from being an open market to being a market in the process of closing up, where the brands have taken their place," he said.
France's cyber-surfers also make little use of the Net, connecting on average two or three times a week for an average of 45 minutes, the study found.
Both the level of equipment and knowledge about multimedia are poor, the study found.
Just over a fifth of those questioned, or 22 percent, knew nothing about multimedia, while another 36 percent had heard of it without really knowing what it was.
Only 12 percent said they knew about multimedia and used multimedia programmes and services either personally or professionally.
Some 23 percent of those questioned own a computer. Of these, 35 percent are equipped with a Pentium chip, 54 percent with a CD-ROM drive and 19 percent with a modem.
Those who want to get into multimedia are not always prepared to spend much on equipping themselves.

The study found just 10 percent were prepared to spend over 10,000 francs to buy a multimedia computer, the usual retail price in France, while 46 percent were prepared to spend 5,000 to 10,000 francs and 44 percent to spend 1,000 to 5,000 francs.
For 61 percent this would be the first time they bought a home computer.
The study questioned 1,001 people, chosen to represent the French population, by telephone between March 12 and March 15.
